title: Debating Ethical Dilemmas / Nkɔso ntɛm nyansa
bridge: Wɔ Twi, sɛ yɛbɛka ho asɛm a, yɛnkyea present tense a ɛfata hɔ a wɔde kyerɛɛ yɛn sɛ yɛbɛka. Wɔ English, subjunctive tense no ara sɛn kyɛn; indicative anaa modal structures no na wɔpɛ. Sɛ yɛka sɛ 'I don't think it is right' a, ɛnte sɛ 'it be right'. Afe a, 'should' ne 'would' a wɔde maa hyɛ adwuma ne conditional sentences no, wɔn sɛn kyɛn wɔ Twi, efisɛ yɛde simple conditional maa hyɛ wɔn. Fa akoma ntow a wɔde kyerɛ adverbials no ne double negation a ɛnyɛ English.
rule: Sɛ wubɛka ho asɛm wɔ English a wɔ B2 level a, hwɛ: 1) 'I think/ believe/ feel' + indicative clause: 'I think that...' (subjunctive no). 2) Modals: 'should' (hyɛ adwuma), 'ought to' (formal), 'must' (hyɛ adwuma paa), 'can't' (ɛnyɛ dɛn), 'could' (ɛyɛ dɛn), 'would' (hypothetical). 3) Agreement/disagreement structures: 'I agree with... because...', 'I see your point, but...', 'That may be true, however...'. 4) Conditionals for ethical hypotheses: 'If we allowed... , then...' (first conditional), 'If I were in that situation, I would...' (second conditional). 5) Connectors: 'therefore', 'moreover', 'nevertheless', 'although'. Fa double negation so ('I don't agree with nothing' ɛnyɛ) ne de inversion maa kyerɛkyerɛ: 'Not only is it unethical, but also...'.

concept_examples.text: I believe that animal testing is unethical because it causes unnecessary suffering.
concept_examples.translation: Mepɛ sɛ animal testing no nyɛ nyansa efisɛ ɛma wɔn ahwɛ a ɛnyɛ dɛn.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ bɪˈliːv ðæt ˈænɪməl ˈtestɪŋ ɪz ʌnˈeθɪkəl bɪˈkɔːz ɪt ˈkɔːzɪz ʌnˈnesəseri ˈsʌfərɪŋ/

concept_examples.text: If I were in that situation, I would tell the truth, even if it was difficult.
concept_examples.translation: Sɛ mɛwɔ hɔ a, mɛkaa nyansa, na ɛno akyi a, ɛyɛ ahwɛ.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɪf aɪ wɜːr ɪn ðæt ˌsɪtʃuˈeɪʃən, aɪ wʊd tɛl ðə truːθ, ˈiːvən ɪf ɪt wʌz ˈdɪfɪkəlt/

concept_examples.phonetic: /wiː ˈʃʊdnt ˈsækrɪfaɪs ˈpraɪvəsi fɔːr sɪˈkjʊrəti; boʊθ ɑːr ɪˈsenʃəl/

common_error.correct: I don't think it is ethical to lie.
common_error.correct_alt: I think it is unethical to lie.
common_error.explanation: Errorkwa baa efisɛ wɔ Twi, double negation (sɛ 'Mɛpɛ sɛ ɛnyɛ nyansa') nea ɛsɛ sɛ yɛbɛka, nanso wɔ English, sentence bi nko na ɛsɛ sɛ ayɛ negation. De nsɛm a ɛfata hɔ no sii anaa de word a ɛfiri so no too so (sɛ 'unethical').

examples.original: From my perspective, this policy has more benefits than drawbacks.

examples.note: Ɛnyɛ sɛ wode 'wɔ me nsa' maa kyerɛɛ sɛn a woka no ho.

examples.original: I couldn't agree more with your argument about renewable energy.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ ˈkʊdnt əˈɡriː mɔːr wɪð jɔːr ˈɑːrɡjumənt əˈbaʊt rɪˈnjuːəbl ˈɛnərdʒi/

examples.original: I see your point, but I think there are other factors to consider.

examples.translation: Mɛhwɛ sɛn a woka no ho, nanso mepɛ sɛ ɛyɛ sɛ ɛyɛ paa akyi a, ɛyɛ ahwɛ.
examples.note: Nsɛm ii maa yɛde ayɛ disagree a ɛnyɛ ahwɛ.

examples.original: That may be true, however, we must also think about the long-term effects.

examples.translation: ɛyɛ sɛ ɛyɛ nyansa, nanso, yɛnsusuw akyi a, ɛyɛ ahwɛ.
examples.note: De 'nevertheless' a ɛba akyi a, ɛyɛ comma.

examples.note: Second conditional maa kyerɛɛ sɛn a ɛnyɛ dɛn anaa ɛyɛ hypothetical. Wɔ English, de 'were' maa kyerɛɛ sɛn a ɛfata hɔ no nyinaa.

examples.original: If I were the CEO, I would prioritize employee well-being over profits.

examples.original: What would you do if you found a wallet with a thousand dollars inside?

examples.note: First conditional maa kyerɛɛ sɛn a ɛyɛ dɛn anaa ɛyɛ probable.

title: Strategic Language for Negotiations / Asɛm a ɛto so ara ne kwan ma wɔde kɔkɔ ne ho asɛm
bridge: Wɔ Twi, yɛnka subjunctive sɛ yɛbɛka sɛ yɛwɔ hɔ ma yɛbɛka sɛ yɛpɛ (’mepɛ’, ’mepɛ sɛ’), nanso wɔ English, wɔnka modals sɛ ’would’, ’could’, ne ’might’ ma wɔayɛ efie a ɛhɔ so, nanso wɔ fa a ɛfata so. Enti, sɛ woaka Twi, ɛsɛ woatwe wo asɛm sɛ wɔ English no so. Ɛsɛ sɛ wotumi aba mu kyɛfa ’de acuerdo’ sɛ ’I am agree’ - ɛbɛyɛ sɛ woka kyerɛw wo ho asɛm.
rule: Wɔ English negotiations a ɛwɔ B2 level no, wɔnka modals ma wɔkɔ so ara ne ma wɔde kwan ma wɔkɔ so (would, could, might, may). Structures sɛ ’I would suggest...’ anaa ’We could consider...’ wɔ hɔ ma wɔde kwan ma wɔkɔ so pɛn pii pɛ ’I want...’ anaa ’You must...’. Ma wɔde kwan ma wɔkɔ so a ɛyɛ den pii, wɔnka ’What if...’ anaa ’How about...’ a ɛbɛka gerund anaa clause. Ma wɔde kwan ma wɔkɔ so a ɛyɛ den pii, wɔnka attenuators sɛ ’I see your point, but...’ anaa ’I’m afraid that...’. Ma wɔde kwan ma wɔkɔ so a ɛyɛ den pii, wɔnka conditionals (If... then...). Yɛnka sɛ wɔ English no, ’agree’ yɛ verb, ɛnyɛ adjective, enti wɔnka ’I am agree’ nanso wɔka ’I agree’.

concept_examples.text: I would suggest we postpone the deadline to next week.
concept_examples.translation: Mɛma wo kyerɛ sɛ mɛbɔ amanneɛ no ahyia nea ɛbɛba akyiri no.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ wʊd səˈdʒɛst wi poʊstˈpoʊn ðə ˈdɛdlaɪn tu nɛkst wik/

concept_examples.phonetic: /wʌt ɪf wi splɪt ðə ˈdɪfərəns ænd mit ɪn ðə ˈmɪdəl/

common_error.wrong: I am agree with your proposal, but we need a better price.
common_error.correct: I agree with your proposal, but we need a better price.
common_error.correct_alt: I completely agree with your proposal, but we would need a better price.
common_error.explanation: Errour no katɔ sɛ wɔ Twi, yɛka ’mewɔ hɔ’ (yɛnka verb ’estar’ + noun), enti wɔde akyire kyɛfa no wɔ English sɛ ’I am agree’. Wɔ English no, ’agree’ yɛ verb a ɛyɛ den pii, ɛnyɛ adjective, enti wɔnka ’to be’ ne so. Ma wode kwan ma wɔkɔ so a ɛyɛ den pii, yɛnka sɛ ’agree’ yɛ ’coincidir’ anaa ’estar de acuerdo’ nanso ɛnyɛ auxiliary ’be’. Yɛnka sɛ ɛsɛ wɔde adverbs sɛ ’completely’ anaa ’partially’ ma wɔde kwan ma wɔkɔ so.

levels.label: Expressing Disagreement Diplomatically
levels.translation: Ma wɔde kwan ma wɔkɔ so a ɛyɛ den pii

examples.original: I see your point, but I have some concerns about the timeline.

examples.original: I'm afraid that's not quite what we had in mind.

examples.translation: Mɛyɛ den sɛ ɛnyɛ nea yɛtɔ so no.
examples.note: ’I’m afraid’ ɛkyerɛkyerɛ fear nanso ɛyɛ polite rejection. Ɛyɛ useful expression.

examples.original: I understand your position, but we would need more flexibility.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ ˌʌndərˈstænd jʊr pəˈzɪʃən bʌt wi wʊd nid mɔr ˌflɛksəˈbɪlɪti/

levels.translation: Ma wɔde kwan ma wɔkɔ so ne ma wɔde kwan ma wɔkɔ so

translations.tw: Asɛm a ɛto so ara ne kwan ma wɔde kɔkɔ ne ho asɛm

title: Discussing Literature and Film / Kasa kɛsɑ̃ Tɛtrɛ ne Sinimɑ
bridge: Wɔ Twirekan ne Sinimɑ ho asɛm bɛka ho, wɔ English a, wɔde 'I found it...' anaa 'It struck me as...' bɛka wɔn ho adwene, na wɔn sɛe wɔ Twi a, yɛde 'me pareció' anaa 'me resultó' bɛka. Anaa, wɔ English a, wɔde adwene-bɔfoɔ no bɛka noun no anim (a gripping novel), na wɔ Twi a, wɔde no bɛka noun no ho (una novela apasionante). Sɛe kɛse bi ara nso ɛha verb tenses a wɔde bɛka story no ho asɛm: wɔ English a, wɔde present simple bɛka story no ho asɛm (the protagonist discovers...), na wɔ Twi a, wɔde present anaa pretérito indefinido bɛka.
rule: Sɛ wopɛ sɛ woka kɛsɑ̃ ne sinimɑ ho asɛm wɔ English a wɔ B2 level no, ɛno ara na wuhia: 1) Ka w'adwene wɔ adjectives ne structures a wɔde bɛka 'I found it + adjective' (I found it thought-provoking) anaa 'It struck me as + adjective' (It struck me as predictable). 2) To story no mu wɔ present simple (The story follows a detective who uncovers a conspiracy). 3) De past simple bɛma events a woka w'akoma ho asɛm (I read the book last year). 4) Compare adaptations wɔ 'unlike' anaa 'whereas' (Unlike the book, the film omits several key scenes). Ɛsɛ sɛ wode 'based on' (The movie is based on a novel). Wɔ vocabulary ho, adjectives a wɔde bɛka 'gripping', 'thought-provoking', 'predictable', 'far-fetched', 'moving' yɛ mfatoho. Mfa 'me pareció' bɛka 'it seemed to me' wɔ nyinaa; de 'I thought' anaa 'I found'.

translations.tw: Kasa kɛsɑ̃ ne Sinimɑ ho asɛm

title: Discussing Health and Science News / Kasa mu nsɛm ne ahoɔden nsɛm
bridge: Wɔ Twiriso, yɛnka akyi a, yɛbɛka deɛ ɛwɔ Hausa kɛ yɛbɛka ahoɔden nkɔsoɔ ne nsɛm a ɛwɔ nnwuma so, na ɛno ara nso yɛde present perfect bɛma ɛkɔm a ɛwɔ akɔsa ne a ɛwɔ akyiri (Researchers have found...) anaa yɛde past simple bɛma ɛkɔm a ɛwɔ nneɛma a wɔayɛle no ho (The study showed...). Enti, wɔ Hausa, wɔde verbs modals bɛka a wɔwɔ hɔ bio a wɔde 'may', 'might' anaa 'could' bɛma ɛkɔm a ɛwɔ ahoɔden ne nnwuma so, na wɔ Twiriso, yɛde 'puede' anaa nneɛma a wɔatwa a wɔwɔ hɔ bio. Nneɛma a ɛne ho hia bio, ɛne deɛ wɔde 'however' ne 'although' bɛma ɛkɔm a ɛwɔ nneɛma a wɔwɔ hɔ bio, na wɔ Twiriso, yɛde 'sin embargo' ne 'aunque' bɛma ɛkɔm a ɛwɔ nneɛma a wɔwɔ hɔ bio, na ɛno ara nso yɛde nneɛma a wɔwɔ hɔ bio ne deɛ wɔde ɛkɔm no so.
rule: Saa wopɛ sɛ woka ahoɔden ne nsɛm a ɛwɔ nnwuma so wɔ Hausa a wɔ B2 level a, ɛno a wode nyinaa: 1) Present perfect bɛma ɛkɔm a ɛwɔ nneɛma a wɔayɛle no ho a ɛwɔ akyiri: 'Scientists have discovered a new vaccine' (Wɔayɛle...), vs. past simple bɛma ɛkɔm a ɛwɔ nneɛma a wɔayɛle no ho: 'The study was published in 2020'. 2) Passive voice bɛma ɛkɔm a ɛwɔ nneɛma a wɔayɛle no ho anaa ɛkɔm no so, na ɛno ara nso ɛnyɛ deɛ wɔde ɛkɔm no so: 'The drug is being tested' (Wɔrekye adwuma no so). 3) Modals a wɔde bɛma ɛkɔm a ɛwɔ ahoɔden so: 'may', 'might', 'could' bɛma ɛkɔm a ɛwɔ ahoɔden so: 'This could lead to new treatments' (ɛno ara nso yɛbɛka ahoɔden). 4) Nneɛma a wɔde bɛma ɛkɔm a ɛwɔ nneɛma a wɔwɔ hɔ bio: 'however' (nanso), 'although' (ɛwɔ hɔ a), 'despite' (ɛwɔ hɔ a), na ɛno ara nso yɛde nneɛma a wɔwɔ hɔ bio (ɛwɔ hɔ a + subject + verb, anaa despite + noun/-ing). 5) Nneɛma a wɔde bɛka wɔ ahoɔden ne nnwuma so: 'evidence', 'findings', 'symptoms', 'treatment', 'effective' vs. 'efficient'. Yɛnka akyi a, yɛbɛka a wɔde pronouns bɛma ɛkɔm a ɛwɔ nneɛma a wɔwɔ hɔ bio: 'The patient whom the doctor treated...' (Deɛ ɔyɛ no ho). Yɛnka akyi a, yɛbɛka a wɔde numbers ne percentages bɛma ɛkɔm a ɛwɔ ahoɔden ne nnwuma so.

concept_examples.text: The study shows that regular exercise can reduce the risk of heart disease.
concept_examples.translation: Nsɛm a wɔkae no ka sɛ, sɛ obi bɔ ne ho ase paa, ɛno ara nso yɛbɛka sɛ ɔbɛyɛ ne ho ban.

concept_examples.text: Scientists have developed a new drug that might slow down the progression of Alzheimer's.

concept_examples.text: Although the results are promising, many experts remain cautious.
concept_examples.translation: ɛwɔ hɔ a nneɛma a wɔayɛle no ho wɔ hɔ, nanso nnipa pii wɔ hɔ a wɔyɛ ne ho ban.

concept_examples.text: The vaccine was tested on thousands of volunteers before being approved.
concept_examples.translation: Wɔde vaccine no hyɛɛ nnipa pii a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde no bɛto frɛ no so.

common_error.wrong: Scientists has discovered a new cure for cancer.
common_error.correct: Scientists have discovered a new cure for cancer.
common_error.explanation: Ɛyɛ ba a wɔde 'have' ne 'has' bɛma ɛkɔm a ɛwɔ nneɛma a wɔwɔ hɔ bio, na wɔ Twiriso, yɛnde 'haber' bɛma ɛkɔm a ɛwɔ nneɛma a wɔwɔ hɔ bio (hemos/han). Enti, sɛ wopɛ sɛ wode 'have' bɛma ɛkɔm a ɛwɔ nneɛma a wɔwɔ hɔ bio a, wo de subject no ne sɛ ɛyɛ plural, na ɛno ara nso yɛde 'has' bɛma ɛkɔm a ɛwɔ third person singular (he/she/it).

levels.label: Understanding medical news
levels.translation: Wɔka nsɛm a ɛwɔ ahoɔden so

examples.original: A recent study has shown that sleep deprivation affects cognitive function.
examples.phonetic: ə ˈrisənt ˈstʌdi hæz ʃoʊn ðæt slip ˌdɛprɪˈveɪʃən əˈfɛkts ˈkɑɡnɪtɪv ˈfʌŋkʃən.
examples.translation: Nsɛm a wɔayɛle no ho ka sɛ, sɛ obi ntumi nna a, ɛno ara nso yɛbɛka sɛ ɔbɛyɛ ne ho ban.
examples.note: Wɔde present perfect ('has shown') bɛma ɛkɔm a ɛwɔ nneɛma a wɔayɛle no ho a ɛwɔ akyiri.

examples.original: Doctors recommend a balanced diet to prevent chronic diseases.
examples.phonetic: ˈdɑktərz ˌrɛkəˈmɛnd ə ˈbælənst ˈdaɪət tu prɪˈvɛnt ˈkrɑnɪk dɪˈzizəz.
examples.translation: Adwuma a wɔyɛ no ka sɛ, sɛ obi bɔ ne ho ase paa, ɛno ara nso yɛbɛka sɛ ɔbɛyɛ ne ho ban.
examples.note: Verb a wɔde bɛka a wɔde bɛto frɛ ('recommend') + noun; wɔ Twiriso, yɛde 'recomiendan' bɛma ɛkɔm a ɛwɔ object a ɛne ho hia bio.

examples.original: The hospital has implemented new protocols to reduce infection rates.
examples.phonetic: ðə ˈhɑspɪtəl hæz ˈɪmpləˌmɛntɪd nu ˈproʊtəˌkɔlz tu rɪˈdus ɪnˈfɛkʃən reɪts.
examples.translation: Hospital no ayɛle nneɛma a ɛbɛyɛ a wɔde bɛto frɛ a ɛbɛyɛ a wɔde bɛto frɛ a ɛwɔ ahoɔden so.
examples.note: Present perfect + 'to' + infinitive a wɔde bɛma ɛkɔm a ɛwɔ nneɛma a wɔwɔ hɔ bio, a ɛne 'para + infinitive' wɔ Twiriso.

examples.original: According to the latest research, there is considerable evidence that climate change affects public health.
examples.phonetic: əˈkɔrdɪŋ tu ðə ˈleɪtəst rɪˈsɜrtʃ, ðɛr ɪz kənˈsɪdərəbəl ˈɛvɪdəns ðæt ˈklaɪmət ʧeɪndʒ əˈfɛkts ˈpʌblɪk hɛlθ.
examples.translation: Nsɛm a wɔkae no ka sɛ, wɔayɛle adwuma a ɛbɛyɛ a wɔde bɛto frɛ a ɛbɛyɛ a wɔde bɛto frɛ a ɛwɔ ahoɔden so.
examples.note: Wɔde 'according to' (nsɛm a wɔkae no) + structure 'there is' bɛma ɛkɔm a ɛwɔ nneɛma a wɔwɔ hɔ bio.

examples.original: The findings suggest that a new treatment could be effective against the virus.

examples.translation: Nsɛm a wɔayɛle no ho ka sɛ, wɔayɛle adwuma a ɛbɛyɛ a wɔde bɛto frɛ a ɛbɛyɛ a wɔde bɛto frɛ a ɛwɔ virus so.
examples.note: Wɔde 'suggest' + 'that' + clause a wɔde verb no so bɛma ɛkɔm a ɛwɔ ahoɔden so (ɛbɛyɛ).

examples.original: However, more research is needed to confirm these results.
examples.phonetic: ˌhaʊˈɛvər, mɔr rɪˈsɜrtʃ ɪz ˈnidɪd tu kənˈfɜrm ðiz rɪˈzʌlts.
examples.translation: Nanso, wɔde adwuma a ɛbɛyɛ a wɔde bɛto frɛ a ɛbɛyɛ a wɔde bɛto frɛ a ɛwɔ ahoɔden so.

examples.original: Although vaccines are widely available, some populations still lack access to them.

examples.original: The government must invest more in public health to avoid future pandemics.
examples.phonetic: ðə ˈgʌvərnmənt mʌst ɪnˈvɛst mɔr ɪn ˈpʌblɪk hɛlθ tu əˈvɔɪd ˈfjuʧər pænˈdɛmɪks.
examples.translation: Government no bebree wɔ ahoɔden so ma wɔde bɛto frɛ a ɛbɛyɛ a wɔde bɛto frɛ a ɛwɔ ahoɔden so.
examples.note: Modal verb 'must' bɛma ɛkɔm a ɛwɔ nneɛma a wɔwɔ hɔ bio; wɔ Twiriso, yɛde 'debe' anaa 'tiene que' bɛma ɛkɔm a ɛwɔ nneɛma a wɔwɔ hɔ bio.

examples.original: Despite the economic costs, the lockdown was necessary to save lives.
examples.phonetic: dɪˈspaɪt ði ˌɛkəˈnɑmɪk kɔsts, ðə ˈlɑkˌdaʊn wʌz ˈnɛsəˌsɛri tu seɪv laɪvz.
examples.translation: ɛwɔ hɔ a nneɛma a wɔayɛle no ho wɔ hɔ, nanso wɔde confinement no hyɛɛ nnipa pii a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde no bɛto frɛ no so.
examples.note: Structure 'despite + noun' (ɛnyɛ clause), a ɛne 'although + clause' a ɛne ho hia bio.

translations.tw: Ahoɔden ne nsɛm a ɛwɔ nnwuma so a ɛyɛ den

title: Discussing Political and Social Issues / Nkɔso ne Nnyɛseɛ Politikal ne Sɛntia
bridge: Wɔ Twi, yɛnkyɛ yɛbɛka ɛkyerɛɛdeɛ wɔ nnyɛseɛ politikal ("Yɛn ho adwuma paa na yɛbɛbɔ ɛkyɛm"). Wɔ Gyeman, afeɛ a wɔka a wɔde adi kan akyi kyerɛɛdeɛ a ɛso nkyɛn wɔ nnyɛseɛ politikal, wɔde 'subjunctive mood' (kyerɛw wɔde ɛkyerɛw) maa 'that' ɛho hɔ: 'It's important that we vote'. Nkyɛnkyɛn bi a ɛso nkyɛn wɔ Twi ne Gyeman: wɔ Twi yɛde ɛkyerɛw a ɛwɔ hɔ wɔ nkyɛn a wɔde 'cuando' ("Cuando haya elecciones"), nanso wɔ Gyeman wɔde ɛkyerɛw a ɛwɔ hɔ: 'When there are elections'. Suhyɛ wɔde 'should' a ɔwɔ hɔ wɔ Twi a ɛdeɛnkyɛma wɔde wɔ nkyɛn a ɛso nkyɛn wɔ Gyeman.
rule: Saa ɛbɛyɛ a wɔbɛka nnyɛseɛ politikal ne sɛntia a ɛwɔ B2, ɛsɛeɛ ne: 1) 'Subjunctive mood' a ɛwɔ hɔ a wɔde adi kan akyi kyerɛɛdeɛ a ɛso nkyɛn wɔ nnyɛseɛ politikal (important, essential, vital, necessary): 'It's essential that the government act now'. Kyerɛw a ɛwɔ hɔ ne sɛ wɔde ɛkyerɛw maa wɔn nyinaa, ɛmmra -s wɔ ɛho. 2) Nkyɛn a ɛwɔ hɔ a wɔde 'when', 'if' ne kondisional: yɛde ɛkyerɛw a ɛwɔ hɔ (ɛmmra ɛkyerɛw a ɛbɛba) wɔ nkyɛn a ɛso nkyɛn: 'When the election happens, we'll know the results'. 3) Kyerɛɛdeɛ a wɔde maa wɔn a wɔyɛ adwuma wɔ nnyɛseɛ politikal: 'I strongly believe', 'I'm afraid I disagree', 'that's a valid point, but...'. 4) Wɔde 'though' maa ɛkyerɛw a ɛwɔ hɔ a wɔde adi kan akyi: 'The policy seems good, though it's expensive'. 5) Nnyɛseɛ a ɛwɔ hɔ wɔ nkyerɛw: 'politics' ne nnyɛseɛ a ɛwɔ hɔ; 'policy' ne nnyɛseɛ bi a ɛwɔ hɔ. Wɔ Twi 'política' ne nnyɛseɛ a ɛwɔ hɔ ne nnyɛseɛ bi a ɛwɔ hɔ, ɛdeɛnkyɛma wɔde wɔ nkyɛn a ɛso nkyɛn wɔ Gyeman.

concept_examples.text: It's crucial that every citizen vote in the upcoming election.
concept_examples.translation: Ɛsɛ sɛ obiara bɛbɔ ɛkyɛm wɔ ɛbɛlabɔlɔ a ɛbɛba mu.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɪts ˈkruːʃəl ðət ˈɛvri ˈsɪtɪzən voʊt ɪn ði ˌʌpˈkʌmɪŋ ɪˈlɛkʃən/

concept_examples.text: When the government takes action, we will see significant changes.
concept_examples.translation: Saa ɛbɛyɛ a ɛbɔneɛm ba, yɛbɛhu ɛho nhyehyɛeɛ.
concept_examples.phonetic: /wɛn ðə ˈɡʌvərnmənt teɪks ˈækʃən wi wɪl si sɪɡˈnɪfɪkənt ˈtʃeɪndʒɪz/

concept_examples.text: Many people argue that the new law is unfair, though it has some advantages.
concept_examples.translation: Mmuaeɛ pii ka sɛ ɛbɔneɛm foforɔ no yɛ ɔkwan a ɛnyɛ adwuma, nanso ɛwɔ adwuma bi a ɛyɛ den.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ˈmɛni ˈpiːpəl ˈɑːrɡjuː ðæt ðə nuː lɔː ɪz ʌnˈfɛr ðoʊ ɪt hæz sʌm ədˈvæntɪdʒɪz/

concept_examples.text: It's essential that the media remain impartial during the campaign.
concept_examples.translation: Ɛsɛ sɛ media no mmra ɛho nhyehyɛeɛ wɔ ɛbɛlabɔlɔ no mu.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɪts ɪˈsɛnʃəl ðət ðə ˈmiːdiə rɪˈmeɪn ɪmˈpɑːrʃəl ˈdʊrɪŋ ðə kæmˈpeɪn/

common_error.wrong: It's important that the government should do something about unemployment.
common_error.correct: It's important that the government do something about unemployment.
common_error.correct_alt: It's important for the government to do something about unemployment.
common_error.explanation: Wɔ Twi, yɛde 'debería' (should) wɔ ɛkyerɛw a ɛwɔ hɔ: 'Yɛn ho adwuma paa na ɛbɔneɛm no debería yɛ den'. Nanso wɔ Gyeman, afeɛ a wɔka a wɔde adi kan akyi kyerɛɛdeɛ a ɛso nkyɛn, wɔde ɛkyerɛw a ɛwɔ hɔ (ɛmmra 'should'): ɛkyerɛw a ɛwɔ hɔ ('do'). Saa ɛbɛyɛ a wɔde 'should', ɛsɛeɛ ne sɛ wɔde ɛkyerɛw foforɔ: 'The government should do something', ɛmmra 'that'. Nkyɛn foforɔ a ɛwɔ hɔ ne 'for + infinitivo'.

examples.original: I strongly believe that education should be a priority for every government.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ ˈstrɔŋli bɪˈliːv ðæt ˌɛdʒuˈkeɪʃən ʃʊd biː ə praɪˈɔrɪti fɔːr ˈɛvri ˈɡʌvərnmənt/
examples.translation: Mepɛ sɛ ɛbɔneɛm no bɛyɛ adwuma a ɛyɛ den wɔ ɛbɔneɛm nyinaa mu.
examples.note: Yɛde 'strongly believe' maa yɛn adwene. Wɔ Twi yɛka 'creo firmemente' nanso suhyɛ: ɛmmra 'I believe strongly' ɛnyɛ adwuma paa.

examples.original: That's a valid point, but I'm afraid I have to disagree with you there.
examples.phonetic: /ðæts ə ˈvælɪd pɔɪnt bʌt aɪm əˈfreɪd aɪ hæv tə ˌdɪsəˈɡriː wɪð juː ðɛr/
examples.translation: Ɛyɛ adwuma a ɛyɛ den, nanso mepɛ sɛ mɛka sɛ mɛyɛ adwuma wɔ ɛho nhyehyɛeɛ.
examples.note: Wɔ Twi, 'me temo que' yɛ ɛkyerɛw a ɛwɔ hɔ: 'me temo que tenga que discrepar'. Wɔ Gyeman yɛde ɛkyerɛw a ɛwɔ hɔ: 'I'm afraid I have to'. Ɛmmra 'I am afraid that I must' (ɛso nkyɛn wɔ Gyeman).

examples.original: I see what you mean, though I think we should look at the bigger picture.

title: Discussing Budgets and Investments / Kasa mu nsusuwnee ne Nkontompo
bridge: Wɔ Twirekan, mmusuo a wɔyɛ de kasa mu nsusuwnee biara rekɔ so ara na ɛsɛe wɔ kwan a wɔkɔ so akasa mu nsusuwnee no ho asɛm. Sɛe wɔ ‘spend’ de gye di mu, nanso ‘invest’ kyerɛ sɛ wɔyɛ nkɔmhyɛ a ɛso awaree pii. Wɔ Twi, yɛde ‘ntompo’ ma obiara mu, nanso wɔ Twirekan, ‘invest’ de ama wɔde nsusuwnee bɔ mu nsusuwnee a obi hwehwɛ sɛ ɔbɔ nea ɔbɔ no mu. Nkɔmhyɛ bi a ɛso awaree pii ne sɛ wɔ Twirekan wɔde mmusuo a ɛso awaree pii de kasa mu nsusuwnee no ho asɛm: ‘invest in’, ‘spend on’, ‘pay for’. Wɔ Twi, wɔmfa mmusuo no ho asɛm maa obiara mu anaa wɔde mmusuo biara maa obiara mu. Fa so ho asɛm yi mu sɛdeɛ ɛbɛyɛ a wɔde wo kwan ma wɔte asɛm no ho asɛm.
rule: Sɛ wopɛ sɛ woka mu nsusuwnee ho asɛm wɔ Twirekan a ɛtɔ so B2, na ɛsɛ sɛ wohu mmusuo ne mmusuo a wɔde kasa mu nsusuwnee no ho asɛm. Mmusuo a wɔde kasa mu nsusuwnee no ho asɛm pii: 'earn', 'save', 'spend', 'invest', 'borrow', 'lend', 'owe', 'pay off', 'set aside'. Mmusuo biara de mmusuo bi a ɛso awaree pii: 'earn money from', 'save up for', 'spend on', 'invest in', 'borrow from', 'lend to'. Mmusuo a wɔde kasa mu nsusuwnee no ho asɛm: 'budget', 'expenses', 'income', 'savings', 'debt', 'interest rate', 'stock market', 'investment portfolio'. De present tense ma woka mu nsusuwnee a woyɛ no ho asɛm ('I save 10% of my income'), na de present perfect ma woka mu nsusuwnee a woyɛe no ho asɛm ('Have you ever invested in stocks?'). Sɛ wopɛ sɛ woma obi nkɔmhyɛ, de 'should' anaa 'ought to'. Hwehwɛ sɛ wɔde 'lend' ne 'borrow' maa wo: 'lend' kyerɛ sɛ wode nsusuwnee ma obi, 'borrow' kyerɛ sɛ wofa nsusuwnee fi obi. Wɔ Twi, 'ntompo' de ma obiara mu, nanso wɔ Twirekan, mmusuo no ho asɛm ni. Enti, 'debt' yɛ mmusuo a ɛnyɛ mmusuo, na wɔmfa 'debts' ma mmusuo a ɛso awaree pii. Sonka sɛ 'money' yɛ mmusuo a ɛnyɛ mmusuo, enti womma 'moneys' maa wo.

title: Expressing Abstract Ideas and Nuance / Kyerɛw Kronkron Adwene ne Nneɛma
bridge: Wɔ Twi, yɛbɛka nneɛma kronkron ne nneɛma a ɛsɛe wɔ subjunctive ne mmoa a wɔkae sɛ 'ɛsɛ sɛ' anaa 'mempa sɛ'. Wɔ English, sɛ wopɛ sɛ woakyerɛwo wo adwene anaa wosɔ hwɛ kwan a efifi so a, wɔdɔm verbs modals ne mmoa a ɛnyɛ den a wɔde bɛka nneɛma a ɛte sɛ wo. Nipa a wɔnnyɛ subjunctive wɔ English, ɛno na ɛsɛ sɛ woatena sɛdeɛ wode bɛkasa gyɛne anaa ɛdeɛn a ɛbɛba so wɔ kwan a ɛyɛ pa. Wo nso sɛ woatɛn nneɛma a wɔte sɛ 'actualmente' (actually) anaa 'realizar' (to realize).
rule:
Sɛ wopɛ sɛ woka kyerɛw kronkron adwene wɔ B2 level wɔ English a, ɛsɛ sɛ wotenam:
1. Verbs modals a wɔde bɛdɔm deduction ne speculation: 'might', 'could', 'may', 'must', 'can't'. Kyerɛw: "She might be right" (ɛsɛ sɛ ɛyɛ nokorɛ) - ɛdeɛn a ɛbɛba so ka wɔ modal, ɛnyɛ subjunctive.
2. Clauses a ɛnyɛ den a wɔde 'it' ka: "It seems that...", "It is said that...", "It is believed that...". Wɔ Twi, yɛde 'se dice', 'se cree', na wɔ English wɔde impersonal passive.
3. Adverbs a wɔde bɛkasa evidence: 'apparently', 'presumably', 'totally', 'completely' ma woka nneɛma kronkron.
4. 'Actually' (nokorɛ) ne 'currently' (sɛe) a wɔte. 'Realize' ka 'to understand', ɛnyɛ 'to do'.
5. Sɛ wopɛ sɛ woka wo adwene a, de 'I would argue that...', 'I tend to think that...', 'From my perspective...'.
6. Hwɛ sɛ wɔmfa 'suggest' ne 'recommend' + that + base form (ɛnyɛ subjunctive): "I suggest that he go" (ɛnyɛ 'goes').
7. 'Would' a wɔde bɛka hypothesis: "If I were you, I would..."

title: Discussing Art and Culture / Kasa mu nsɛm ne akwanmu
bridge: Wɔ Twi, yɛnka ɛno a ɛte saa wɔ Espaniol, yɛnka ɛno a ɛte saa wɔ Twi. Wɔ Twi, yɛnka 'present perfect' (have seen) sɛnea yɛbɛka ɛno a ɛte saa wɔ Espaniol, na yɛnka 'past simple' sɛnea yɛbɛka ɛno a ɛte saa wɔ Twi. Sɛnea yɛbɛka ɛno a ɛte saa wɔ Twi, yɛnka ɛno a ɛte saa wɔ Espaniol, nanso yɛbɛyɛ ɛno a ɛte saa wɔ Twi. Wɔ Twi, yɛnka 'the' sɛnea yɛbɛka ɛno a ɛte saa wɔ Espaniol, na yɛnka ɛno a ɛte saa wɔ Twi.
rule:
Saa ɛbɛyɛ a wɔbɛka kasa mu nsɛm ne akwanmu wɔ Twi a ɛte saa B2, ɛsɛ: 
- Yɛnka ɛno a ɛte saa wɔ Twi: 'The painting depicts...'
- Yɛnka 'present perfect' sɛnea yɛbɛka ɛno a ɛte saa wɔ Twi: 'I have visited the Prado Museum.'
- Yɛnka 'past simple' sɛnea yɛbɛka ɛno a ɛte saa wɔ Twi: 'She painted this in 1990.'
- Adjetivos: ɛno a ɛte saa wɔ Twi (opinión, tamaño, edad, material, origen) ne yɛnka 'so' ne 'such' sɛnea yɛbɛka ɛno a ɛte saa wɔ Twi.
- Kasa mu nsɛm: 'In my view...', 'It strikes me as...'
- Verbos modales sɛnea yɛbɛka ɛno a ɛte saa wɔ Twi: 'It might be a fake.', 'It could represent freedom.'

title: Problem-solving discussions / Nkɔso ntɛm nyansapɔm
bridge: Wɔ Twi, sɛ yɛbɛka ho nhia a, yɛnkyɛn yɛbɛka ‘sɛ mɛto wo a’ anaa ‘ɛnhyɛ sɛ...?’. Nkyɛnkyɛnka, wɔ English, wɔdɔn modal ne conditional structures a wɔwɔ hɔ paa. Ɛyɛ den a wɔde ‘si yo sería’ ka ‘if I were’ (second conditional). Enti, wɔ English, wɔpɛ ‘should’ ne ‘ought to’ sɛ wɔbɛma obi akɔso, nkyɛnkyɛnka wɔ Twi, ‘deberías’ yɛ direct paa. Fa akwantu no so klaa ne ‘would’ a wɔde wɔ main clause no ho.
rule:
Sɛ wubɛka nkɔso ne ma akɔso wɔ English a, wɔdɔn structures yi: 
1. **Second Conditional** (hypothetical): 'If + simple past, would + base verb'. Kyekye: 'If we had more time, we could finish the project.' Wɔdɔ no wɔ hypothetical anaa unlikely situations. 
2. **Third Conditional** (past hypothetical): 'If + past perfect, would have + past participle'. Kyekye: 'If we had known earlier, we would have solved it.' Wɔdɔ no ka past opportunities a wɔayɛ. 
3. **Recommendation Modals**: 'should', 'ought to', 'had better' + base verb. 'Had better' yɛ strong ne wɔma ɛho asɛm biara. 
4. **Phrases for proposing ideas**: 'What about...?', 'How about...?', 'Why don't we...?', 'Could we...?', 'Maybe we should...'. 
5. **Expressions for evaluating options**: 'On the one hand... on the other hand...', 'The advantage is...', 'The downside is...', 'It might work because...'. 
6. **Agreements and disagreements**: 'I see your point, but...', 'That sounds reasonable, however...', 'I'm not convinced that...'. 
Mfa ‘would’ wɔ ‘if’ clause no (common error wɔ Spanish speakers).

title: Talking about Goals and Ambitions / Kasa mu nsusuwne ne nneɛma wɔ opɛ mu
bridge: Wɔ Twi mu, yɛnkye yɛbɛka ɛno a, yɛde asɛm a ɛte saa ara na yɛde ma yɛbɛka yɛn nsusuwne ne yɛn nneɛma wɔ opɛ mu. Nanso, wɔ English mu, ɛsɛ sɛ yɛde asɛm a ɛte saa ara na yɛde ma yɛbɛka yɛn nsusuwne, te sɛ ‘I’m planning to’, ‘I intend to’, anaa yɛde ‘will’ ma yɛbɛka yɛn nneɛma a yɛbɛyɛ wɔ ɔkwan bi mu. Sɛnea yɛbɛka ‘would like’ (me gustaría) wɔ English mu nso, ɛte sɛnea yɛbɛka ‘quiero’ wɔ Twi mu, efisɛ ɛbɛka nneɛma a yɛpɛ sɛ yɛbɛyɛ wɔ ɔkwan bi mu.
rule: Sɛ wopɛ sɛ wɔbɛka wo nsusuwne ne wo nneɛma wɔ opɛ mu wɔ English mu a, wɔde nneɛma bi ma wɔbɛka: 1) ‘be going to + infinitive’ sɛ wopɛ sɛ wɔbɛka nneɛma a wopɛ sɛ wɔbɛyɛ wɔ ɔkwan bi mu (I’m going to start a business). 2) ‘will + infinitive’ sɛ wopɛ sɛ wɔbɛka nneɛma a wopɛ sɛ wɔbɛyɛ wɔ ɔkwan bi mu anaa sɛ wopɛ sɛ wɔbɛka nneɛma a wɔbɛyɛ wɔ ɔkwan bi mu (I’ll do my best). 3) ‘would like + infinitive’ anaa ‘would love + infinitive’ sɛ wopɛ sɛ wɔbɛka nneɛma a wopɛ sɛ wɔbɛyɛ wɔ ɔkwan bi mu (I’d like to improve my English). 4) Mmusuo te sɛ ‘hope’, ‘plan’, ‘intend’, ‘expect’ a wɔde ma wɔbɛka infinitive (I hope to travel, I plan to save money). 5) Asɛm a wɔde gerund ma wɔbɛka akyi: ‘look forward to + -ing’, ‘be interested in + -ing’. 6) First conditional sɛ wopɛ sɛ wɔbɛka nsusuwne a ɛne baabi a: ‘If I study hard, I’ll pass the exam’. Nneɛma a ɛsɛ sɛ wo ntwe: wɔnkye ‘to’ wɔ infinitives mu, wɔde infinitive ma wɔbɛka akyi prepositions (correct: ‘I’m good at learning’), ne sɛ wɔde ‘will’ ne present tense ma wɔbɛka nsusuwne a ɛyɛ den. Wo nso, hwɛ sɛ ‘hope’ bɛka akyi present simple sɛ ɛbɛka nneɛma a ɛbɛyɛ wɔ ɔkwan bi mu (I hope I get the job).

examples.original: I’m going to start a new hobby this summer.
examples.phonetic: /aɪm ˈɡoʊɪŋ tə stɑːrt ə nuː ˈhɑːbi ðɪs ˈsʌmər/
examples.translation: Mɛto wo mma wɔ m’abusua baabi a.
examples.note: Yɛde ‘be going to’ ma yɛbɛka nsusuwne a yɛayɛe wɔ ɔkwan bi mu akyi.

examples.original: I intend to apply for that job in London.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ ɪnˈtend tə əˈplaɪ fɔːr ðæt dʒɑːb ɪn ˈlʌndən/
examples.translation: Mepɛ sɛ mɛto wo mma wɔ London.
examples.note: Mmusuo ‘intend’ de ‘to + infinitive’ akyi. Ɛyɛ paa wɔ kasa mu wɔ ‘going to’ mu.

examples.original: I’m hoping to save enough money for a trip.
examples.phonetic: /aɪm ˈhoʊpɪŋ tə seɪv ɪˈnʌf ˈmʌni fɔːr ə trɪp/
examples.translation: Mepɛ sɛ mɛto wo mma wɔ m’abusua baabi a.
examples.note: Sɛ wode ‘hope’ a, ɛbɛka akyi present continuous sɛ ɛbɛka nsusuwne a ɛyɛ den.

examples.original: I plan to learn Spanish next year.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ plæn tə lɜːrn ˈspænɪʃ nekst jɪr/
examples.translation: Mɛto wo mma wɔ m’abusua baabi a.
examples.note: ‘Plan to’ de infinitive akyi na yɛde ma yɛbɛka nsusuwne a ɛyɛ den.

examples.original: If I get a promotion, I’ll buy a house.
examples.phonetic: /ɪf aɪ ɡet ə prəˈmoʊʃən aɪl baɪ ə haʊs/
examples.translation: Sɛ mɛtoa m’nsusuwne a, mɛto wo mma.
examples.note: First conditional wɔ English mu: if + present, will + infinitive. Yɛnkye yɛde future tense wɔ ‘if’ clause mu.

examples.original: Unless I start saving now, I won’t be able to travel.
examples.phonetic: /ənˈles aɪ stɑːrt ˈseɪvɪŋ naʊ aɪ woʊnt bi ˈeɪbəl tə ˈtrævəl/
examples.translation: Sɛ mɛnto wo mma a, mɛnto wo mma.
examples.note: ‘Unless’ te sɛ ‘sɛ’ na ɛde negations akyi, entɔ yɛnkye yɛde ‘not’ wɔ clause no mu.

examples.original: Provided that I finish my thesis, I’ll graduate in June.
examples.phonetic: /prəˈvaɪdɪd ðæt aɪ ˈfɪnɪʃ maɪ ˈθiːsɪs aɪl ˈɡrædʒueɪt ɪn dʒuːn/
examples.translation: Sɛ mɛtoa m’nsusuwne a, mɛtoa m’akwantuanso wɔ June.
examples.note: ‘Provided that’ yɛ paa wɔ kasa mu wɔ ‘if’ mu na ɛte sɛ ‘sɛ’.

examples.original: Once I have enough experience, I’ll start my own company.
examples.phonetic: /wʌns aɪ hæv ɪˈnʌf ɪkˈspɪriəns aɪl stɑːrt maɪ oʊn ˈkʌmpəni/
examples.translation: Sɛ mɛtoa m’nsusuwne a, mɛto wo mma.
examples.note: Yɛde ‘once’ + present sɛ yɛbɛka nneɛma a ɛbɛyɛ wɔ ɔkwan bi mu, ɛte sɛ ‘sɛ’.

levels.label: Discussing Ambitions
levels.translation: Kasa mu nneɛma wɔ opɛ mu

examples.original: I would love to become a successful writer.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ wʊd lʌv tə bɪˈkʌm ə səkˈsesfəl ˈraɪtər/
examples.translation: Mepɛ sɛ mɛyɛ akwantufoɔ a ɔyɛ den.
examples.note: ‘Would love to’ yɛ paa wɔ kasa mu wɔ ‘would like to’ mu na yɛde ma yɛbɛka nsusuwne a ɛyɛ den.

examples.original: My dream is to travel around the world and help communities.
examples.phonetic: /maɪ driːm ɪz tə ˈtrævəl əˈraʊnd ðə wɜːrld ənd help kəˈmjuːnətiz/
examples.translation: M’nsusuwne yɛ sɛ mɛto wo mma ne mɛkɔ so.
examples.note: Sɛ nsusuwne no yɛ subject a, yɛde ‘is to + infinitive’ ma yɛbɛka nsusuwne no.

examples.original: I’m working towards becoming a certified coach.
examples.phonetic: /aɪm ˈwɜːrkɪŋ təˈwɔːrdz bɪˈkʌmɪŋ ə ˈsɜːrtɪfaɪd koʊtʃ/
examples.translation: Mepɛ sɛ mɛyɛ akwantufoɔ a ɔyɛ den.
examples.note: Yɛde ‘work towards’ ma yɛbɛka gerund efisɛ ‘towards’ yɛ preposition.

examples.original: In ten years’ time, I hope to have my own practice.
examples.phonetic: /ɪn ten jɪrz taɪm aɪ hoʊp tə hæv maɪ oʊn ˈpræktɪs/
examples.translation: Wɔ ɛno a, mepɛ sɛ mɛtoa m’akwantuanso.
examples.note: Yɛde ‘in + period + time’ sɛ yɛbɛka ɔkwan a ɛbɛyɛ wɔ ɔkwan bi mu.

translations.tw: Nsusuwne ne nneɛma wɔ opɛ mu
